description: Retrospective discussion of the crop, livestock or soft’s own price: session settles, limit up and limit down moves, contract highs and lows, cash and auction prices, and explanation of a move that has happened.
Forward-looking views: agency and government crop estimates, balance sheet and carryout projections, crop tour and yield forecasts, and analyst price targets.

Relative value and traded exposure: calendar and inter-commodity spreads, crush and blending margins, cash basis, old crop against new crop, volatility and options, open interest, managed money and commercial positioning, and technical analysis such as chart levels and momentum signals.
Relevant Agriculture market mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
The economic backdrop for food demand: food price inflation, interest rates and recession risk, income growth and general economic health in consuming markets.
Currency moves changing export competitiveness, farmer selling incentives and local prices in producing and importing countries.
War and conflict disrupting production or trade routes, diplomatic tension, and political instability in producing or exporting regions.
Domestic agricultural policy and rules: farm bills and subsidies, minimum support prices, phytosanitary and food safety standards, pesticide approvals and land use policy.

Cross-border measures affecting agricultural trade: import tariffs and duties, export taxes and bans, quotas and licensing, anti-dumping cases, trade wars and retaliation, sanctions and trade agreements.
Mandates and rulings driving biofuel demand: blending obligations and volume targets, waivers and exemptions, tax credits, and renewable fuel policy.
Relevant Agriculture macro mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Field supply: planting and intentions, acreage, crop progress and condition, phenology, harvest pace, yield estimates and production totals.
Timber supply from forests and mills: logging and harvest activity, lumber and wood output, forestry production totals, and changes to land available for commercial timber extraction.
Animal supply: herd and flock size, breeding and farrowing intentions, slaughter rates and carcass weights, milk output per cow and dairy production, and culling decisions.
Growing and grazing conditions: drought, rainfall and monsoon, frost and freeze, heat waves and heat stress, flooding, El Nino and La Nina, and crop condition ratings.
Biological loss: animal disease and culls, quarantine and movement restrictions, pests and infestations, fungal disease and blight, and contamination incidents.
Volumes held and the reports that measure them: ending stocks and carryout, quarterly stocks, cold storage holdings, on-feed inventories, and warehouse and port stocks.
Interruption to production and movement: barge, rail and truck problems, river levels, port and canal closures, strikes, plant fires and outages, and supply chain failure.
Relevant Agriculture supply mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Buying interest from major importing regions: state and private purchase programmes, import tenders, reserve building and shifts between origins.
Transactional demand news: daily and weekly export sales, tender issues and awards, private bookings, cancellations and offers.
Measured movement: export inspections, customs data, shipments and cargo loadings, line-ups and physical trade flows.
Physical processing and industrial usage: ethanol and biodiesel production, soybean and rapeseed crush, sugar milling and refining, and the run rates and margins driving them.
Animal consumption: feed and meal demand, feedlot placements, ration substitution between grains, and livestock market trends driving feed usage.
Commercial demand for purchased agricultural inputs such as fertilizer, crop nutrients and soil treatments, including producer adoption and usage growth.
End-consumer demand: retail food and beverage prices, grocery and foodservice trends, and consumption of softs such as coffee, sugar and cocoa.
Relevant Agriculture demand mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Processor, trader, packer and producer results, guidance and margins.
M&A, divestitures, capacity investment, plant acquisitions, joint ventures and strategic pivots.
Relevant Agriculture corporate mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Retrospective discussion of allowance and credit price action: settlements, highs and lows, records, technical levels, and explanation of a move that has happened.
Forward-looking views: price forecasts and targets, supply-demand balance and scarcity projections, and analyst views on scheme tightness.

How the carbon market is organised and traded: curve structure and carry, spreads, positioning, open interest, liquidity, technical analysis, and the market infrastructure that makes trading possible — registries, tracking systems, permit processing, exchanges and trading access.
Relevant Carbon market mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.

The contest over the rules before they are settled: elections and coalition positions, national resistance or ambition, international negotiations, industry lobbying and public pressure shaping the direction of a scheme.

Scheme design, the law that sets it, and enforcement of those rules: trading phases and targets, directives and legislation, linking between schemes, sector coverage, carbon taxes, price floors, border adjustments, participant bans, fines, fraud investigations, and regulatory suspensions of permit or registry processes.
Relevant Carbon macro mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
How many units exist: the cap and its trajectory, free allocation and benchmarks, allocation to new entrants, cross-sectoral correction factors, and the scarcity that results.
Primary market release: auction calendars and volumes, results and clearing prices, bid cover ratios, undersubscription, cancellations and failed auctions.
Mechanisms that withhold, release or destroy units: stability reserve intake and release, backloading, invalidation and cancellation of surplus, and equivalent supply management in other schemes.
Units from outside the cap: project credits and their issuance, eligibility rules and qualitative restrictions, credit prices, and voluntary market units.
Relevant Carbon supply mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.

Obligation-driven buying: surrender deadlines and compliance events, verified emissions reporting, the size of covered entities’ obligations, and utility and industrial forward hedging of allowance needs.

The abatement stack in power: coal-to-gas switching economics, relative fuel prices setting the switching price, generation mix and the weather-driven load behind it, and the allowance demand that follows.

Output and emissions from covered sectors: industrial production and activity levels, the economic cycle driving them, decarbonisation and abatement investment, plant closures, and carbon leakage concerns.
Relevant Carbon demand mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Retrospective discussion of the crude, product or gas price itself: settles, highs and lows, benchmark assessments, records, and after-the-fact explanation of a move.
Forward-looking views: agency, bank and consultancy demand and supply forecasts, balance projections and price targets.

Relative value and traded exposure: crack and refining margins, time spreads, contango and backwardation, regional and quality differentials, arbitrage economics, fund positioning, open interest, hedging programmes, and technical analysis such as chart levels and momentum signals.
Relevant Energy market mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Macroeconomic conditions setting consumption: central bank decisions, interest rates, inflation data, GDP and recession signals, and currency moves.
Political risk and diplomacy short of violence: negotiations and nuclear or supply deals, diplomatic tension, alliances and summits, elections, coups, unrest and resource nationalism.
Violence threatening supply: war, attacks on tankers, terminals and infrastructure, drone and missile strikes, militancy, seizures and blockades.
Government energy policy and rules: climate mandates, emissions and sulphur standards, blending rules, drilling and pipeline permits, taxation, ESG rules and strategic energy plans.

State restrictions and incentives on cross-border energy trade: sanctions, embargoes, price caps, export licensing and waivers, tariffs and duties, quotas, anti-dumping cases, trade wars and retaliation, and trade agreements.
Coordinated supply management: producer group quotas and cuts, compliance with agreements, output pacts and unilateral production discipline.
Relevant Energy macro mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Upstream activity: rig counts, well completions, shale productivity, field and platform start-ups, liquefaction trains, and upstream investment converting into supply.
Downstream conversion: refinery and cracker run rates and utilisation, scheduled turnarounds and maintenance, new capacity and closures, and yield shifts between products.
Unplanned loss of supply: refinery and platform outages, pipeline failures, storms and hurricanes, fires, explosions, strikes and force majeure.
Volumes held: crude and product stockpile reports, gas in storage, days of cover, floating storage, and strategic reserve builds and releases.
The physical system and its use: pipelines, terminals and storage facilities, tanker movements and loadings, exports and imports, arrivals and cargo diversions.
Relevant Energy supply mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Aggregate demand: total and regional consumption figures, demand growth estimates, and import and export volumes used as a demand proxy.
Fuel burned for movement: driving season and mileage, aviation and jet demand, trucking and freight activity, and marine and bunker consumption.
Fuel burned by industry and generators: manufacturing consumption, gas and oil power burn, utility fuel choice and procurement.
Feedstock demand: cracker operating rates and feedstock selection, olefin margins, and plastics and derivative demand pulling naphtha, LPG and ethane.
Weather-driven consumption: heating and cooling demand, cold snaps and mild winters, degree days and seasonal load, and weather-driven storage draws.
Relevant Energy demand mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Producer and refiner results, guidance, margins, dividends and impairments.
M&A, asset sales, farm-ins, final investment decisions, capex programmes, partnerships and long-term supply contracts.
Relevant Energy corporate mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Retrospective discussion of freight rates and index levels: route and vessel-class rates, index moves, records, and explanation of a move that has happened.
Forward-looking views: rate, tonne-mile and fleet balance forecasts, and analyst views on the freight cycle.

Relative value and traded exposure: forward freight agreements against spot, route and vessel-class differentials, period against prompt rates, paper market positioning and liquidity, and technical analysis such as chart levels and momentum signals.
Relevant Freight market mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.

Global trade volumes and the measures that move them: import and export growth, the trade cycle, tariffs and duties, trade wars and retaliation, trade agreements, and trade patterns lengthening or shortening voyages.
War risk and political disruption to shipping: attacks on vessels, piracy, sanctions on cargoes, owners or flags, blockades, and conflict closing or reopening trade lanes.

Rules governing ships and their emissions: fuel sulphur limits and specification changes, carbon and efficiency rules, ballast water and safety regulation, port state control, and flag and registry rules.
Relevant Freight macro mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.

Vessel capacity: orderbook and newbuilding contracting, deliveries, demolition and recycling, fleet growth, idle and laid-up tonnage, slow steaming, and scrubber retrofitting taking ships off the water.

Fuel for ships: bunker prices and spreads between grades, fuel specification changes and compliance fuel switching, scrubber economics, and bunker availability at ports. Bunker fuel is the largest voyage cost and sits directly inside the rate.

Insurance costs and availability for shipping: hull and machinery, protection and indemnity, cargo and war-risk premiums, surcharges, exclusions, and changes in cover that alter vessel operating costs or route economics.

Effective port and route capacity: structural port, terminal and canal works including construction, expansion, dredging, cranes and automation; and the friction that absorbs that capacity — congestion, queues, waiting time, berth availability, loading delays, weather disruption at port, transit restrictions, draft limits and rerouting.
Relevant Freight supply mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Cargo volumes moved and sought: iron ore, coal, grain and minor bulk shipments, crude and product cargoes, floating storage economics, stockpiling cycles and tonne-mile demand.
How tonnage is committed: fixtures and period charters, contract of affreightment coverage, charterer appetite, forward cover and enquiry levels.
Relevant Freight demand mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Owner and operator results, guidance, vessel operating costs, solvency, restructuring and bankruptcy.
M&A, newbuilding orders, sale and purchase of vessels, consolidation, pool formation and strategic reviews.
Relevant Freight corporate mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Retrospective discussion of the metal’s own price: session settles, highs and lows, multi-period records, and after-the-fact explanation of a move that has happened.
Forward-looking price views: bank and consultancy forecasts and price targets, target revisions, supply-demand balance projections and rating changes.

Relative value and traded exposure: futures curve and contango or backwardation, spreads, basis, regional and physical premiums, options and volatility, open interest, speculative positioning, ETF holdings, and technical analysis such as chart levels and momentum signals.
Relevant Metals market mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Central bank decisions, interest rate moves, monetary policy and governor commentary, including the real yield channel that reprices non-yielding metals.
Data on the state of the economy: CPI and PPI inflation, GDP and growth, manufacturing and industrial output, PMIs and employment.
Government intervention to lift activity: fiscal packages and budgets, infrastructure and construction programmes, credit easing, property support and subsidies for metal-intensive sectors.
Currency moves and FX volatility repricing metal for buyers outside the pricing currency, and producer-currency moves changing local cost and selling incentives.
War, terrorism, attacks, diplomatic tension, international relations, elections, unrest, resource nationalism and expropriation affecting metal supply or risk premium.
Mining and permitting policy, environmental and safety rules, royalties and taxes, export controls, and strategic stockpile policy.
Cross-border measures: tariffs and duties, anti-dumping and countervailing cases, quotas, safeguards, sanctions, embargoes and trade disputes affecting metal flows.
Relevant Metals macro mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Primary output from the ground: production reports and guidance, ore grades, reserves, exploration findings, new mines, ramp-ups and expansions.
Midstream conversion: smelter and refinery capacity and utilisation, scheduled maintenance, treatment and refining charges, concentrate availability, and mill output.
Secondary supply: scrap availability and collection rates, scrap spreads and discounts to primary metal, recycling capacity, and rules governing scrap grades and imports.
Metal held and moved: exchange and regional stockpiles, bonded and social inventories, warehouse levels, imports and exports, and physical shipments.
Unplanned loss and interruption: strikes, accidents, fires, power outages, weather, protests and blockades at mines and plants, and transport, port and rail disruption.
Relevant Metals supply mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Metal consumed by construction and general industry: property and infrastructure activity, power grid build-out, electronics and manufacturing demand.
Metal consumed by vehicles and the energy transition: automotive production and sales, EVs, batteries and cathode material, solar and wind components, and emissions catalysts.
Consumer fabrication and retail: jewellery demand, bar and coin buying, festival and wedding season purchasing, and physical retail premiums.
Metal bought as a store of value: ETF inflows and outflows, central bank and official sector purchases, coin and bar demand, and safe-haven or inflation hedging.
Utility fuel buying: coal burn for generation, reactor restarts and nuclear fuel demand, and utility procurement or stockpiling ahead of season.
Relevant Metals demand mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Producer financial performance: results, guidance, margins, cost reports, impairments and dividends.
Ownership and capital allocation: M&A, divestitures, stakes, buybacks, joint ventures, capex guidance, project financing and strategic pivots.
Relevant Metals corporate mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Retrospective discussion of spot, day-ahead, balancing and forward power prices: settlements, spikes, negative prices, records, and explanation of a move that has happened.
Forward-looking views: price, load, margin and adequacy forecasts, seasonal outlooks and reserve margin assessments.

Relative value and traded exposure: spark and dark spreads, clean spreads after carbon, peak against baseload, spreads between connected markets, traded positioning and liquidity, and technical analysis such as chart levels and momentum signals.
Relevant Power market mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Economic activity driving electricity consumption: industrial output, manufacturing activity, employment and recession signals.
Discretionary government action on power prices: price caps and freezes, windfall levies, consumer bill support and subsidies, state aid, and public and political pressure over energy costs.
Structural market rules: market design and reform, capacity mechanisms and auction rules, network codes, licensing, support schemes for generation, and environmental and emissions regulation.
Relevant Power macro mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Fossil-fired output: coal, gas and oil-fired generation levels, running hours, dispatch and merit order position, and plant availability in the thermal fleet.
Wind and solar output: generation levels and records, renewable share of the mix, build-out and grid connection, curtailment, and intermittency events.
Reactor availability: planned and extended outages, restarts after inspection, uprates, lifetime extensions, closures and nuclear policy decisions.
Hydro conditions and output: reservoir and snowpack levels, inflows, hydrological balance and hydro generation.
Unplanned loss of generation: plant trips and forced outages, accidents, fires, sabotage and emergency shutdowns.

The network: transmission and distribution, interconnector flows, capacity and availability, cross-border trade, congestion and constraints, balancing and frequency, curtailment for network reasons, blackouts, and storage on the system.
Changes to the asset base: new build and commissioning, retirements, mothballing and phase-outs, capacity auctions and awards, and investment decisions.
Input costs setting marginal cost: gas, coal and oil prices to generators, carbon and allowance costs, fuel supply contracts, and the switching economics between fuels.
Relevant Power supply mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Measured consumption: system load and peak demand, industrial, commercial and residential offtake, demand response and load records.
Meteorological conditions and forecasts driving load and renewable output: temperature, cold snaps and heatwaves, wind and cloud conditions, rainfall and seasonal patterns.
Structural demand growth: EV charging, heat pumps, data centres, industrial electrification, and efficiency changing the demand base.
Relevant Power demand mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
Utility and generator results, guidance, margins and impairments.
M&A, asset sales, project investment, power purchase agreements, partnerships and strategic reviews.
Relevant Power corporate mechanisms that belong to this branch but do not fit any named L2 topic.
